population: 68 patients with advanced Parkinson's disease, carbidopa 4:1, tablets and intestinal gel
blocking_issue: None for the curve.  Two compartments, absorbed through one transit compartment (the paper's own simulated peaks need two steps); motor effect site from Mao 2013, which was fitted to observed concentrations and so sits on any plasma model.  Valid at carbidopa 4:1 only; no sex or age term (age p = 0.0057, not included).
source: Othman AA, Dutta S. Population pharmacokinetics of levodopa in subjects with advanced Parkinson's disease: levodopa-carbidopa intestinal gel infusion vs. oral tablets. Br J Clin Pharmacol 2014;78:94-105. PMID 24433449, PMC4168384; reproduced in the FDA Clinical Pharmacology Review of NDA 203952.

population: 27 patients with advanced Parkinson's disease, IR carbidopa-levodopa and IPX066
blocking_issue: The pharmacodynamic half of the levodopa model: UPDRS III ke0 1.80/h (equilibration half-life 0.39 h), EC50 812 ng/mL, Hill 2.5, maximal improvement 63%; tapping ke0 1.17/h, EC50 1590 ng/mL; dyskinesia ke0 1.55/h, EC50 601 ng/mL.  Advanced disease only: equilibration is far slower in early disease.
source: Mao Z, Hsu A, Gupta S, Modi NB. Population pharmacodynamics of IPX066: an oral extended-release capsule formulation of carbidopa-levodopa, and immediate-release carbidopa-levodopa in patients with advanced Parkinson's disease. J Clin Pharmacol 2013;53:523-531. PMID 23426902, PMC3798100.

population: 45 patients with advanced Parkinson's disease on intestinal gel
blocking_issue: None for the curve.  Transit rate 9.2/h and bioavailability 0.97 relative to tablets; the gel's doses and its continuous enteral rate run through the transit compartment exactly (R/transit.R).
source: Othman AA, Dutta S. Br J Clin Pharmacol 2014;78:94-105 (as above), and FDA CDER Clinical Pharmacology Review, NDA 203952 (Duopa), 2015.

population: early Parkinson's disease (study 248.524) with healthy volunteers and renal impairment
blocking_issue: None for the curve.  The creatinine clearance formula is not stated (Cockcroft-Gault used); V3 is printed for the ER tablet and taken for both; doses are the dihydrochloride monohydrate, the model's base (salt / 1.431), confirmed by reproducing the reviewers' simulated AUCs to 0.3%.
source: FDA CDER. Clinical Pharmacology and Biopharmaceutics Review, NDA 22-421 (Mirapex ER), 2009: Boehringer Ingelheim's population model, Table 3.

population: early Parkinson's disease on ER tablets (study 248.524)
blocking_issue: None for the curve.  The ER tablet's sequential zero- (1.34 h) and first-order (0.0873/h) absorption on the pramipexole disposition.
source: FDA CDER. Clinical Pharmacology and Biopharmaceutics Review, NDA 22-421 (Mirapex ER), 2009, Table 3.

population: 1171 patients with Parkinson's disease in three phase 3 studies
blocking_issue: None for the curve.  The covariate equations are not printed; the power forms reproduce the review's stated ranges.  White patients' relative bioavailability (1.04) is used; no race field.
source: FDA CDER. Clinical Pharmacology Review, NDA 207145 (Xadago), Pharmacometrics Review, Table 1 (sponsor Model 136).

population: 724 subjects in 21 studies (3 in Parkinson's disease), fasting
blocking_issue: Plasma only: COMT inhibition outlasts the drug by days.  Fixed at the label's bedtime micronised capsule without levodopa; F1 joined through the 25 and 50 mg strengths by a power; bilirubin held at 12 umol/L; the transit structure inferred as levodopa's.
source: FDA CDER. Clinical Pharmacology Review, NDA 212489 (Ongentys), 2020, Table 9 (sponsor population model 2018-CP-198).

population: 1449 subjects (1219 with Parkinson's disease) in 16 studies
blocking_issue: None for the curve.  Lean body mass is not defined (James used); smoking (x1.63 CL) and CYP3A4 inhibitors (x0.736) have no Patient Profile field and are held at none.  Read from the 2007-8 FDA pharmacometrics review, Table 1; the paper itself was read as the abstract.
to_obtain: Knebel W, Rao N, Uchimura T, et al. Population pharmacokinetic analysis of istradefylline in healthy subjects and in patients with Parkinson's disease. J Clin Pharmacol 2011;51:40-52. PMID 20200269 (full text, to confirm the lean body mass equation).
source: Knebel W et al. J Clin Pharmacol 2011;51:40-52, as Table 1 of the FDA pharmacometrics review in the Clinical Pharmacology Review of NDA 022075 (Nourianz), 2019.

population: 24 adults with normal, moderately and severely impaired renal function, one 160 mg HCl tablet
blocking_issue: The input structure is inferred (79.9% first order, 20.1% zero order over 8.79 h into the central compartment); it reproduces the normal and severe groups and under-predicts the moderate group's AUC by 43%.  24 subjects, single doses; doses as HCl in the model, converted from the label's base.
source: FDA CDER. Clinical Pharmacology Review, NDA 209410 (Osmolex ER), 2017, Reviewer Analysis, Table 6.

population: patients with Parkinson's disease psychosis (troughs), absorption from healthy volunteers
blocking_issue: None for the curve.  Doses as tartrate in the model, converted from the label's base; the active metabolite AC-279 is not modelled; the single-dose peak is later than measured because the absorption was fixed from troughs.
source: FDA CDER. Clinical Pharmacology Review, NDA 207318 (Nuplazid), 2016, Pharmacometrics Review, Table 6 (sponsor's selected Stage 3 model).

population: Japanese patients with Parkinson's disease, 25-50 mg/day
blocking_issue: Already in the library as an antiseizure drug (R/drugs_zonisamide.R), and it stays in that category.  Its model is linear, so it scales to the Parkinson's doses, at which its antiseizure band does not apply.
to_obtain: Murata M, Hasegawa K, Kanazawa I, et al. Zonisamide improves wearing-off in Parkinson's disease: a randomized, double-blind study. Mov Disord 2015;30:1343-1350. PMID 26094993.
source: Murata M et al. Mov Disord 2015;30:1343-1350.

population: 623 patients with Parkinson's disease (studies 015 and 016)
blocking_issue: Complete (CL/F 3.59 L/h, V/F 120 L, ka 0.582/h, allometric weight, F 0.724 for study 016), but the authors suspect a mesylate-versus-base dosing error between their two studies, and its ka puts the peak at 5 h against the label's 2-3 h.  The FDA's Model 136 is used instead.
source: Loprete L, Leuratti C, Cattaneo C, et al. Population pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic analyses of safinamide in subjects with Parkinson's disease. Pharmacol Res Perspect 2016;4:e00251. PMID 27713822, PMC5045937.

population: patients with Parkinson's disease psychosis (troughs)
blocking_issue: Complete alternative: CL/F 588.814 L/day x (1 + 0.00853 (height - 168)) x (1 + 0.00486 (CKD-EPI - 72)), V/F 2007 L.  Its objective function was lower, but the sponsor judged the renal term physiologically unrealistic and selected Table 6.
source: FDA CDER. Clinical Pharmacology Review, NDA 207318 (Nuplazid), 2016, Table 7.

population: healthy subjects, single and multiple doses of ADS-5102
blocking_issue: One compartment with a lag (the reviewer's medians V 522 L, ka 0.368/h, lag 3.41 h, k10 0.0359/h), but these are statistics of individual two-stage fits, not a population model, the review's text and table disagree on ka and k10, and the renal term is only implied by a table (k10 = 0.0003 CrCl + 0.00122, a rescaled literature regression).  Too weak to plot beside the Osmolex model.
to_obtain: Hauser RA, Pahwa R, Wargin WA, et al. Pharmacokinetics of ADS-5102 (amantadine) extended release capsules administered once daily at bedtime for the treatment of dyskinesia. Clin Pharmacokinet 2019;58:77-88. PMID 29777529, PMC6325984 (its parameter tables).
source: FDA CDER. Clinical Pharmacology Review, NDA 208944 (Gocovri), 2017, Tables 2, 4 and 5.

population: 352 patients with early Parkinson's disease (TEMPO), 1 or 2 mg/day
blocking_issue: Complete (two compartments: ka 6.20/h and V3/F 3300 L fixed, CL/F 58.5 L/h x (WT/70)^0.541 x (AGE/60)^-0.403 x 0.69 with levodopa, V2/F 125 L x (AGE/60)^-0.785, Q/F 46.4 L/h), but the apparent clearance falls 3-4 fold from the first dose (225 L/h) to steady state (70 L/h; PRESTO), the reviewers judged the 1 mg data of low quality, the levodopa term contradicts the label, and the effect is irreversible MAO-B inhibition, which plasma does not predict.
source: FDA CDER. Clinical Pharmacology Review, NDA 021641 (Azilect), Pharmacometrics, Table 7.1.16.

population: 11 patients with advanced Parkinson's disease, levodopa-carbidopa and levodopa-entacapone-carbidopa intestinal gel on consecutive days
blocking_issue: None for the curve.  One compartment (Table 2): CL/F 27.9 L/h x (WT/70)^0.75 on levodopa-carbidopa gel, 36.5% lower (17.7 L/h) on levodopa-entacapone-carbidopa gel (Lecigon), Vc/F 74.5 L x WT/70, ka fixed at 50/h; the weight exponents fixed.  Only the Lecigon arm is a drug, since levodopaIntestinalGel already carries Othman's gel model, which the LCIG arm corroborates.  COMT rs4680 and DDC genotypes compared only graphically (11 patients): no trend by COMT, a tendency to higher clearance with higher DDC activity; no genotype term.  Motor effect site from Mao 2013.
source: Senek M, Nyholm D, Nielsen EI. Population pharmacokinetics of levodopa gel infusion in Parkinson's disease: effects of entacapone infusion and genetic polymorphism. Sci Rep 2020;10:18057. PMID 33093598, PMC7582154.

population: 30 patients with advanced Parkinson's disease and peak-dose dyskinesia (Hoehn and Yahr 3-4), single 150% doses after a 12-h washout
blocking_issue: None for the curve.  One compartment, no lag (Table 2): ka 1.86/h, CL/F 36.6 L/h x (WT/70)^0.75, V/F 42.9 L x WT/70, the allometry fixed (no covariate survived); one effect compartment for both effects (Table 3, model 2): ke0 1.37/h, UPDRS III E0 31.4, Emax 72%, EC50 1410 ng/mL, Hill 4.26; dyskinesia Emax 17.9, EC50 6280 ng/mL.  The authors' predictive check underpredicts the peak, and sampling ended at 5 h.  A second levodopa beside Othman's plasma and Mao's effect site: one study, its effect site fitted on its own plasma model, in later, dyskinetic disease.
source: Simon N, Viallet F, Boulamery A, Eusebio A, Gayraud D, Azulay J-P. A combined pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic model of levodopa motor response and dyskinesia in Parkinson's disease patients. Eur J Clin Pharmacol 2016;72:423-430. PMID 26936272.

population: 71 patients and volunteers on IPX066 (Rytary)
blocking_issue: One compartment (CL/F 56.8 L/h, V/F 114 L) with three parallel lagged first-order absorption phases (27, 48 and 25% of the dose), whose three rate constants and lags the review does not print.
to_obtain: The sponsor's population pharmacokinetic report for NDA 203312 (Impax), or a publication of its parameters; FDA CDER Clinical Pharmacology Review, NDA 203312.
source: FDA CDER. Clinical Pharmacology Review, NDA 203312 (Rytary), 2015.

population: healthy volunteers on IR, CR and IPX203 (Crexont)
blocking_issue: A population model with a dual depot for IPX203; its parameters are not in the abstract, which quotes an 'expected therapeutic range (750-1000 ng/mL)'.
to_obtain: Wach A et al. J Neural Transm 2026, doi:10.1007/s00702-026-03233-w (full text). PMID 42479139.
source: Wach A, Kopra J, Marjanovic I, Knecht M, Jenner P. Population pharmacokinetic analyses comparing immediate-release levodopa/carbidopa, controlled-release levodopa/carbidopa, and IPX203. J Neural Transm 2026.

population: 18 healthy subjects and 19 patients with motor fluctuations on dissolved levodopa-carbidopa microtablets (Flexilev), single doses
blocking_issue: Complete (Table 2): two compartments, CL/F 1.31 L/min x (WT/70)^0.75 / (1 + carbidopa dose / 86.7 mg) (48.5 L/h at 50 mg carbidopa, 40 L/h at 75 mg), Vc/F 45.4 L, Q/F 0.667 L/min, Vp/F 44.9 L, Hoehn and Yahr on CL/F (-0.0616), age on F (0.00172); the double peak as two parallel absorption chains, 74.9% with a mean transit time of 16.1 min and the rest 86.2 min, through five and six transit compartments (the paper does not say which chain has which).  The engine carries one transit compartment, and the clearance depends on the carbidopa dose of the occasion, which the dose table does not carry; the model over-predicts the first doses of a multiple-dose study.  Microtablets are not marketed in the US.
source: Senek M, Nyholm D, Nielsen EI. Population pharmacokinetics of levodopa/carbidopa microtablets in healthy subjects and Parkinson's disease patients. Eur J Clin Pharmacol 2018;74:1299-1307. PMID 29882153, PMC6132549.

population: patients with early (EASE-PD Monotherapy) and advanced (EASE-PD Adjunct) Parkinson's disease on ropinirole IR and 24-hour prolonged release
blocking_issue: Read in full: one compartment with first-order absorption from two depots (a bolus for IR, a zero-order input for the prolonged release), one shared ka, sex, age, weight, BMI, stage and hormone replacement tested on clearance; but the paper prints no parameter estimate, only the exposure-response logistic regressions.  The label's CL/F (47 L/h), volume (7.5 L/kg) and half-life (6 h) are mutually inconsistent and give no ka, so no model is built from them.
to_obtain: The population model of ropinirole prolonged release (studies 101468/164 and 165; Tompson's reference 3), or the FDA Clinical Pharmacology Reviews of NDA 020658 and NDA 022008.
source: Tompson D, Oliver-Willwong R. Pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic comparison of ropinirole 24-hour prolonged release and ropinirole immediate release in patients with Parkinson's disease. Clin Neuropharmacol 2009;32:140-148. PMID 18978485.

population: 6 patients with idiopathic Parkinson's disease, single SC doses of 2-10 mg on three days (study APOM0073)
blocking_issue: None for the curve.  The FDA pharmacometrics review (scanned, read in full): one compartment, ka 14.9/h, CL/F 191 L/h, V/F 153 L; inhibitory sigmoid Emax on an effect compartment, ke0 5.36/h, EC50 10.7 ng/mL, B0 24.3, Emax 1 and Hill 3 fixed.  Nasser 2024 (read in full with its correction and supplement) uses exactly these numbers to compare SC with sublingual apomorphine, and its simulated SC peak (11 min, 5.28 ng/mL per mg) is reproduced.  Six patients and no covariate; doses as the hydrochloride, the label strength.
source: FDA CDER. Clinical Pharmacology and Biopharmaceutics Review, NDA 21-264 (Apokyn), Appendix II Pharmacometrics Review, 2004; Nasser A et al. Model-based comparison of subcutaneous versus sublingual apomorphine administration in the treatment of motor fluctuations in Parkinson's disease. J Pharmacokinet Pharmacodyn 2024;51:385-393. PMID 38578533.

population: patients with Parkinson's disease, SC and intranasal
blocking_issue: One compartment in the abstract (V 1.74 L/kg, kel 1.53/h, ka 23.0/h SC and 20.5/h intranasal), not checked against the full text.
to_obtain: Neef C, Jelliffe RW, van Laar T, et al. Int J Biomed Comput 1994;36:143-148. PMID 7927855 (full text).
source: Neef C et al. Int J Biomed Comput 1994;36:143-148.

population: 8 healthy men, 20 mg IV 13C-entacapone with 100 mg oral
blocking_issue: Read in full: the intravenous disposition is complete (Table 1, means of individual three-compartment fits: Vc 0.08 L/kg, k10 9.68/h, k12 2.15, k21 2.43, k13 0.69, k31 0.44/h; CL 11.7 mL/min/kg, Vss 0.27 L/kg), but 'the absorption phase could not be analysed adequately': only tmax 0.9 h, Cmax 457 ng/mL and F 25% after 100 mg.  On this disposition no first-order absorption without a lag peaks later than 15 minutes, so the oral route, the only clinical one, would need an invented lag and rate.
to_obtain: Keranen T, Gordin A, Karlsson M, et al. Inhibition of soluble catechol-O-methyltransferase and single-dose pharmacokinetics after oral and intravenous administration of entacapone. Eur J Clin Pharmacol 1994;46:151-157. PMID 8039535 (an oral two-compartment fit); or the EMA EPAR for Comtess.
source: Heikkinen H, Saraheimo M, Antila S, Ottoila P, Pentikainen PJ. Pharmacokinetics of entacapone, a peripherally acting catechol-O-methyltransferase inhibitor, in man. A study using a stable isotope technique. Eur J Clin Pharmacol 2001;56:821-826. PMID 11294372.

population: 215 fluctuating patients with Parkinson's disease, 50-400 mg three times daily (sparse steady-state samples)
blocking_issue: None for the curve.  Fluctuator model (Table 3): two compartments, CL 4.8 L/h x (LBW/55)^0.73, Vc 16 L x (LBW/55)^0.65, Q 5.2 L/h, Vp 12 L, ka 1.7/h, no lag, F 0.6 fixed from the intravenous study, so absolute parameters.  Serum protein on CL and albumin on Vp held at the medians (no Patient Profile field), and the dose factor on both volumes (0.55 at 50 mg, 1.40 at 400 mg) at the 200 mg reference; food (F x 0.88) not applied.  The nonfluctuator model (60 patients: CL 4.5 L/h x (CLcr/68)^1.19, Vc 3.5 L, Vp 24 L, Q 7.7 L/h, ka 0.7/h, lag 0.4 h) is the paper's alternative.
source: Jorga K, Fotteler B, Banken L, Snell P, Steimer J-L. Population pharmacokinetics of tolcapone in parkinsonian patients in dose finding studies. Br J Clin Pharmacol 2000;49:39-48. PMID 10606836.

population: 16 healthy young men, 200 mg oral and 50 mg IV crossover
blocking_issue: Complete (Table 2, means of individual two-compartment fits with first-order absorption: Vc 4.9 L, Vss 9.0 L, CL 7.3 L/h, distribution half-life 0.2 h, ka 1.1/h, lag 0.5 h, F 0.7; COMT inhibition EC50 1.2 mcg/mL).  Healthy young volunteers, whose total volume is a third of the patients' (28 L), so the patients' model (Jorga 2000) is the one drawn; this study is its absolute-bioavailability anchor (F 0.6 by AUC) and its check: the patients' clearance is 66% of the volunteers'.
source: Jorga KM, Fotteler B, Heizmann P, Zurcher G. Pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics after oral and intravenous administration of tolcapone, a novel adjunct to Parkinson's disease therapy. Eur J Clin Pharmacol 1998;54:443-447. PMID 9754991.

population: 6 healthy adults, 8 patients with renal insufficiency and 10 on haemodialysis, one 300 mg dose of amantadine HCl
blocking_issue: Read in full: individual one-compartment fits with a lag, but only half-lives are printed (11.8 h in the healthy, 18.5-812 h in renal insufficiency, 8.3 days on dialysis, which removes under 5% of a dose), with no volume, absorption rate or lag for the reference group, in whole blood (16% above plasma), and a regression of the elimination rate on measured 24-h creatinine clearance (k = -0.002752 + 0.000666 CrCl per 1.73 m2; the printed plus sign is a misprint, as the text and Table 2 show) from eight patients at CrCl 6-43.  Closing a model would need a volume digitised from Figure 1A.  It is the independent check on amantadineER's renal scaling: 10.9 h at CrCl 100 and 66 h at 20, against the ER model's 14.6 h at eGFR 100 and 69 h at 21.
to_obtain: A full-text population model of immediate-release amantadine; Aoki FY, Sitar DS. Clin Pharmacol Ther 1985;37:137-144. PMID 3967456.
source: Horadam VW, Sharp JG, Smilack JD, et al. Pharmacokinetics of amantadine hydrochloride in subjects with normal and impaired renal function. Ann Intern Med 1981;94:454-458. PMID 7212501.

population: 18 healthy subjects and 19 patients on dissolved microtablets
blocking_issue: Complete (Table 2): one compartment, CL/F 1.05 L/min x (WT/70)^0.75 (63 L/h; -1.19% per year of age, +1.41% per Hoehn and Yahr stage), V/F 168 L x WT/70 (half-life 111 min), two parallel absorption chains (57.0% with a mean transit time of 34.6 min, the rest 121 min, 19% longer in women) through three and ten transit compartments.  The chains exceed what the engine carries.  Carbidopa is not plotted: its role is to make levodopa's model valid.
source: Senek M, Nyholm D, Nielsen EI. Eur J Clin Pharmacol 2018;74:1299-1307. PMID 29882153.

population: 11 patients with Alzheimer's disease, 6 mg oral and 2 mg IV over 1 h crossover
blocking_issue: Read in full and set aside as an incoherent table: two compartments with Michaelis-Menten elimination, a lagged oral depot and F 0.60 (Table IV: Vmax 125 ug/L/h, Km 2.0 ug/L, Vc 44.9 L, ka 2.0/h, k23 2.9/h, k32 1.22/h, lag 0.44 h), but under neither reading of Vmax's units (a concentration rate, or an amount) does the printed set reproduce the paper's own measurements (IV Cmax 16.3 ug/L, AUC 37 ug.h/L; oral Cmax 25.6, AUC 71; half-life 1.4-1.7 h): it misses by up to fifteenfold, with a 3% variability on Vmax.  The dose basis (tartrate or base) is not stated, no covariate was tested, and the population is Alzheimer's, not Parkinson's, dementia.
source: Hossain M, Jhee SS, Shiovitz T, et al. Estimation of the absolute bioavailability of rivastigmine in patients with mild to moderate dementia of the Alzheimer's type. Clin Pharmacokinet 2002;41:225-234. PMID 11929322.

population: 158 healthy subjects and patients with Parkinson's disease, SC (Apokyn) and sublingual (Kynmobi)
blocking_issue: Complete and checked (CL/F 80.7 L/h, V2/F 438 L x (WT/69.3)^1.53, k26 0.613/h, k62 0.0048/h; ka SC 17.6/h and SL 6.58/h, each through two transit compartments; SL bioavailability 0.91 x 0.202 relative to SC), reproducing the paper's simulated Cmax and AUC.  The engine carries one transit compartment, not two, and the deep compartment (return half-life 144 h) accumulates artificially over days, so the model is valid for single or same-day doses and not for the infusion.
source: Agbo F, Crass RL, Chiu YY, et al. Population pharmacokinetic analysis of apomorphine sublingual film or subcutaneous apomorphine in healthy subjects and patients with Parkinson's disease. Clin Transl Sci 2021;14:1464-1475. PMID 33650272, PMC8301595.

population: patients with neurogenic orthostatic hypotension
blocking_issue: Two compartments (CL/F 702 L/day, V1 40.8 L, Q/F 130 L/day, V2/F 178 L; levodopa-carbidopa factor 0.528 on CL) with an inverse Gaussian absorption (mean absorption time 0.241 day, shape 0.658), which the engine lacks, and an age term ('0.8% per year after 65') whose form is not printed.
to_obtain: The functional form of the age term (the sponsor's population report for NDA 203202).
source: FDA CDER. Clinical Pharmacology Review, NDA 203202 (Northera), 2014, Table 1.

population: the Neupro label
blocking_issue: Transdermal: about 45% of the patch content released in 24 h, lag 3 h, peak 15-18 h; the engine has no transdermal route.
source: Neupro (rotigotine transdermal system) prescribing information.

population: patients with Parkinson's disease, 84 mg inhaled, on oral carbidopa
blocking_issue: Non-compartmental only (tmax 30 min, half-life 2.3 h, V/F 168 L, about 70% of oral exposure), and the engine has no pulmonary route.
source: FDA CDER. Clinical Pharmacology Review, NDA 209184 (Inbrija), 2018.

population: patients on foslevodopa-foscarbidopa SC infusion
blocking_issue: The FDA review has no population model; the measured steady states by dose fix the clearance but not the subcutaneous absorption or the prodrug's bioavailability, and the library has no mass-rate SC infusion unit.
to_obtain: Rosebraugh M et al. (AbbVie) population pharmacokinetics of levodopa from foslevodopa-foscarbidopa, when published.
source: FDA CDER. Clinical Pharmacology Review, NDA 216962 (Vyalev).

population: the Eldepryl and Zelapar labels
blocking_issue: No compartmental model: the kinetics are nonlinear and time-dependent (half-life 2 h after one dose, 10 h at steady state; exposure x2.7 from day 1 to day 8), bioavailability 4-10% and tripled by food, and the effect is irreversible MAO-B inhibition, which the label says plasma does not predict.
source: Eldepryl (selegiline hydrochloride) prescribing information; Mahmood I. Clin Pharmacokinet 1997;33:91-102.

population: 1034 patients in five phase 2/3 studies (resubmission)
blocking_issue: The 2019 model's intercompartmental clearance is unidentified (Q/F 0.92 L/h, SE 1044%) and its covariate forms and reference values are not printed; Knebel 2011 is used instead.
source: FDA CDER. Clinical Pharmacology Review, NDA 022075 (Nourianz), 2019, Table 5.

population: the Parlodel and Cycloset labels
blocking_issue: Non-compartmental values only (tmax 2.5 h, half-life 5 h, Cmax 465 pg/mL after 5 mg); no population model was found.
source: Parlodel (bromocriptine mesylate) prescribing information.

population: the Dostinex label
blocking_issue: Non-compartmental values only (tmax 2-3 h, half-life 63-69 h); no population model was found, and it is not approved for Parkinson's disease in the US.
source: Dostinex (cabergoline) prescribing information; Del Dotto P, Bonuccelli U. Clin Pharmacokinet 2003;42:633-645.

population: none read
blocking_issue: Reported approved by the FDA in September 2026 (news only); neither the label nor a population model was found.
to_obtain: The Juvmo prescribing information and FDA Clinical Pharmacology Review, when posted.
source: AbbVie. Tavapadon (Juvmo); approval reported 28 September 2026.

population: 8 healthy men, 4 mg
blocking_issue: Cmax 7.2 ng/mL, tmax 1.3 h, ka 2.07/h, but no volume or clearance; other studies' half-lives (3.7 to 10 h) disagree.  No population model exists.
source: He H, McKay G, Wirshing B, Midha KK. Development of a sensitive and specific radioimmunoassay for trihexyphenidyl. J Pharm Sci 1995;84:561-567.

population: none
blocking_issue: No human pharmacokinetic study beyond an assay method and overdose case series.
source: Fahy P, Arnold P, Curry SC, Bond R. Serial serum drug concentrations and prolonged anticholinergic toxicity after benztropine (Cogentin) overdose. Am J Emerg Med 1989;7:199-202.

population: 6 healthy subjects, IV and oral
blocking_issue: Biphasic (half-lives 1.5 and 24 h, CL 12 mL/min/kg, V 24 L/kg, oral F 33%) without the intercepts that would fix a model; not marketed in the US.
source: Grimaldi R, Perucca E, Ruberto G, et al. Pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic studies following the intravenous and oral administration of the antiparkinsonian drug biperiden to normal subjects. Eur J Clin Pharmacol 1986;29:735-737.

population: none
blocking_issue: A European dopamine agonist (Trivastal), not approved in the US; nothing could be read here.
to_obtain: A national (European) product information for Trivastal, or a population model of piribedil.
source: Trivastal (piribedil) product information.
